title: Why is Northwind's renewal at risk? Competing hypotheses
caption: ACH matrix, Heuer inconsistency tally. Evidence E1–E6 from Q2 account review; E6 non-diagnostic (neutral against all). n=5 hypotheses x 6 evidence.

hypotheses.label: Price sensitivity
hypotheses.description: Northwind balks at the 18% renewal uplift and is shopping on cost.

hypotheses.label: Product gaps
hypotheses.description: Missing SSO/SCIM and reporting features block their expansion use case.

hypotheses.label: Champion left
hypotheses.description: Their executive sponsor departed in March; no internal advocate remains.

hypotheses.label: Competitor displacement
hypotheses.description: A rival vendor ran an active POC inside the account.

hypotheses.label: Low adoption
hypotheses.description: Seats were under-utilized; the product never reached daily-active critical mass.

evidence.text: Procurement requested a line-item discount and a multi-year cost schedule.
Three support tickets cite missing SCIM provisioning and custom report exports.
Sponsor (VP Ops) LinkedIn shows a role change to a different company in March.
Weekly active users fell from 140 to 38 over two quarters.
A competitor's logo appeared on a shared screen during a recent QBR.
Northwind's overall headcount grew 12% year over year.

semantic_description.level_1_elemental: A 6-row by 5-column ACH grid. Rows are evidence items E1-E6; columns are five competing hypotheses H1-H5 for why the Northwind renewal is at risk. Each cell holds a consistency code from CC, C, N, I, II, or NA. Each evidence row carries credibility and relevance ratings (H/M/L); E6 (headcount growth) is non-diagnostic, neutral against every hypothesis.
semantic_description.level_2_statistical: Heuer inconsistency tally weights I and II marks against each hypothesis. H1 carries the only inconsistency, a strong one (E4 = II, the usage collapse strongly contradicts simple price-shopping); H2, H3, H4, H5 carry zero inconsistencies. By the discriminating-disconfirmation logic of ACH, H1 is the weakest and the other four survive.
semantic_description.level_3_perceptual: The strong-consistent (CC) cells fall on a near-diagonal: each surviving hypothesis owns one anchor evidence row (E2->H2, E3->H3, E5->H4, E4->H5). E4 (usage collapse) reads hot across the row, consistent-or-stronger for four hypotheses but strongly inconsistent for H1, the matrix's one decisive disconfirmation. The all-neutral E6 row and the single NA cell read as flat gaps rather than support.
semantic_description.level_4_contextual: No hypothesis is fully eliminated, but H1 (pure price sensitivity) is effectively ruled out; the survivors point to product gaps plus a lost champion driving low adoption rather than cost alone.
semantic_description.short_alt: ACH grid, 6 evidence x 5 renewal hypotheses; usage-collapse strongly contradicts price-sensitivity, leaving product-gaps and lost-champion.
